title: Escarpment and Summit
premise: Lena Marchetti, a storm chaser deep in debt to a predatory adventure-tourism syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover equipment abandoned by a vanished government survey team in a remote monsoon-battered river gorge. With the help of Tomas, a quiet ferryman whose family once held the concession she now needs to survive, she discovers the survey team didn't vanish—they were run off by the syndicate's enforcers, and the permits expire with the monsoon's end. Betrayed by her own employer and stranded by floodwater, Lena must choose between selling out Tomas's inheritance to clear her debt or burning her records and testifying, ending with her surrendering the salvage, the syndicate exposed, and Lena staying through one full season for the first time in twenty years.
about_author: Elodie Iversen is a former river guide who spent a decade running monsoon-season logistics in Southeast Asia before turning to writing full time. She lives in a converted boathouse and still checks barometric pressure compulsively.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Opening on a chase run through Kansas hail, we learn she measures life in miles and owes the Vantage syndicate a crushing salvage debt. A contract offer arrives: recover a government survey team's abandoned gear from the Kalyet Gorge before concession permits expire. Emotional beat: restless escape dressed up as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Gorge Keeps Its Own Records
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She reaches the river town of Sarn Khol and finds the survey camp intact—gear stowed, meals half-eaten, no tracks, no bodies. Locals go silent when she asks questions. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession as she realizes the disappearance is deliberate, not accidental.

chapters.title: A Stranger With a Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The ferryman Tomas agrees to take Lena upriver, though his boat leaks and his family's concession papers are the very ones expiring. He knows who scared off the survey team but says nothing yet. Emotional beat: two guarded people negotiating trust through shared labor on the water.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season Has No Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The rains trap them at a mid-river camp. Inventorying the salvage, Lena finds the survey team's real cargo: evidence that Vantage falsified concession records to strip the Khol family's rights. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of what she's carrying—and for whom.

chapters.title: The Optimists Send a Letter
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A syndicate enforcer arrives by raft, polite and smiling, offering to buy the salvage and forgive Lena's debt if she hands over the survey evidence and abandons Tomas. Lena stalls. Emotional beat: loyalty and self-preservation pulling in opposite directions for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Water Takes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A flash flood destroys half the salvage and nearly drowns Tomas; Lena saves him, wrecking the enforcer's raft and burning her own exit option. Stranded together, Tomas finally reveals the survey team fled alive and hid the evidence with his family. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in catastrophe.

chapters.title: Inheritance Is a Debt You Didn't Sign
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In the Khol family shrine, Tomas shows Lena the hidden survey records proving the concession fraud. He asks her to testify; she calculates that testimony means prison-adjacent ruin while the debt follows her forever. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging made explicit.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying Invisible
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The syndicate's enforcers close in as the permits near expiry; Lena attempts a solo night run downriver with the evidence to trade it quietly for her freedom. The plan collapses—she can't make the handoff without Tomas's knowledge of the river. Emotional beat: the loneliness strategy failing on its own terms.

chapters.title: Summit of the Concession
chapters.summary: Lena and Tomas's alternating POV. Climax: they run the flooded gorge together to reach the land registry before permits lapse, outmaneuvering the enforcers, and Lena publicly files the survey evidence and her testimony instead of the salvage claim. Vantage's fraud unravels; her debt dies with the syndicate's contracts. Emotional beat: choosing truth over the clean exit.

chapters.title: One Full Season
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weeks later, the gorge quiets, the Khol concession is restored, and the survey team's fate is resolved with the survivors found upstream. Lena repairs Tomas's boat instead of buying a ticket out. Emotional beat: resolution—she stays, measuring life for once in seasons, not miles.
